scope: Limited primary-source foundations for a static funded capped-GBM mean-square hedge and convex KKT. This is not a complete literature-priority review.

sources.title: Convex Optimization
sources.publication_type: Published textbook, not a journal article.
sources.actual_version: Author-hosted published-book PDF; the author page states that Cambridge University Press permits free web access.
sources.consulted_scope: Section 4.2.3, pp. 139–140, inequalities (4.20)–(4.21); Section 5.2.3, pp. 226–227, refined Slater qualification; Sections 5.5.2–5.5.3, pp. 242–245, complementary slackness, KKT and equality-constrained quadratic example; Section 5.8.3 Farkas lemma, p. 263; normal-cone definition in Exercise 2.38(c), p. 66. Central KKT pages inspected visually.
sources.claim_supported: Established convex first-order optimality, affine-constraint duality/KKT, normal-cone definition and finite-dimensional quadratic programming.
sources.not_supported: An exercise defining normal cones is not itself a completed polyhedral normal-cone proof. The project must derive its active-set representation, degeneracies and numerical error statement. Book results do not confer a new financial model or originality.

sources.title: Convex duality in mean-variance hedging under convex trading constraints
sources.actual_version: Final publisher journal PDF, journal-paginated 1084–1112 and bearing Applied Probability Trust copyright. Journal issue is December 2012; the later Cambridge platform publication date is not the original journal year.
sources.consulted_scope: Introduction and Section 2, pp. 1084–1088: discounted wealth, fixed-versus-optimised initial capital, constrained mean-square loss. Section 4, p. 1095, Theorem 4.1 and proof, inspected visually. General semimartingale closedness and duality machinery in Sections 3 and 5 were not fully read or independently verified.
sources.claim_supported: Established fixed-capital mean-square hedging and convex trading constraints, distinguished from optimising the initial capital and from unrestricted pricing.
sources.not_supported: The source studies dynamic predictable semimartingale strategies. This project restricts holdings to a finite static terminal basis, proves existence directly, and does not implement the general dynamic/duality theorem or local risk minimisation. No transfer of unverified closedness assumptions.

sources.title: Optimal static quadratic hedging
sources.publication_type: Published peer-reviewed journal successor, with an explicitly identified pre-publication body consulted.
sources.actual_version: arXiv:1506.02074v2, posted 19 November 2015; manuscript title page dated 20 November 2015. This is a pre-publication version, not represented as the accepted or final journal body. Final article publication details and abstract were verified in Safari and Crossref.
sources.consulted_scope: Section 2, manuscript pp. 3–4, equations (2.1)–(2.2); Section 3.2, pp. 11–12, Assumption 3.5, Proposition 3.6, equations (3.24)–(3.27); Appendix A, pp. 26–27. Finite-asset proposition and Appendix A inspected visually.
sources.claim_supported: Closest antecedent: physical-measure expected squared static hedging error, pricing-measure cost, finite tradable basis, raw payoff moment matrices and a cost-constrained quadratic programme.
sources.not_supported: The consulted model assumes zero interest and no dividends and permits signed holdings with one cost constraint. The project must derive dividend reinvestment and funded-gain accounting, additional long-only/position constraints and its own numerical checks. The static QP is an established method, not a new theory. Final-body textual identity or literature priority is not established.

access_summary: The paper-index search was attempted and failed DNS resolution; no paid access or entitlement acquired.
Final Cambridge journal PDF and author-hosted optimisation textbook read freely.
Final Leung–Lorig metadata/abstract checked in Safari; actual body consulted is named arXiv v2.
financial_distinctions: Loss is under P; initial claim and hedge prices are stipulated no-arbitrage Q prices.
Initial capital V0 is fixed, not optimised to produce a minimum-variance price.
For dividend reinvestment into stock, g_S=exp((q-r)T)S_T-S0. Fixed-share/cash-dividend gains are a different path-dependent convention.
With fixed funded capital, the moment matrix is E_P[gg^T], not Cov_P(g), unless the relevant P means actually vanish.
The Black–Scholes–Merton model is dynamically complete; the allowed static instrument set can fail to span the capped payoff.
A static terminal decision is not a dynamic/local-risk-minimising strategy, a Monte Carlo prediction control, or a new quantum algorithm.
comparison_conclusion: Established quadratic hedging and convex optimisation supply the method. The project-specific value is transparent funded/dividend accounting, checked moments and constraints, matched comparisons and retained synthetic evidence. No theoretical priority or empirical market adequacy is claimed.
